summary: Judge A rated the note sound; judge B flagged the opening 'superseding' paragraph as a scope gap. I kept B's gap but corrected its finding: that paragraph does say the imported recovery algorithm is not implemented, but it states the removal of the prime-conductor opening without the condition that the known-norm note's local application of Theorem 1.3 is review pending, which the closing section concedes. Both judges agreed on, and I re-checked, the technical core: brute-force projective counts at (p,d)=(7,3),(13,3),(13,4),(11,5) equal p^2+p+1+C with B=(d-1)(d^2-3d+3) terms of modulus p, and the primary congruence held on 1398 prime-conductor triples. The artifact confirms 14 controls, 1032 triple records, 64/64 balanced LLL rows, 246 phase checks, the six d in {3,5,7} completed reconstructions, and the 61-bit point count equal to p^2+p+1+C with |C|<=910p.

claims.quote: Under the stated Jacobi/primary identities this removes the prime-conductor asymptotic quantum opening
claims.finding: The headline paragraph states the removal as established, while it rests on JACOBI_KNOWN_NORM_REDUCTION's local application of Lenstra-Silverberg Theorem 1.3, which is review pending (artifact flags local_reduction_independently_or_formally_reviewed=false); this note's closing section says 'Independent review of the local application is still needed'. The paragraph does already state that the imported recovery algorithm is not implemented here.

claims.quote: Character orthogonality gives this projective formula
claims.finding: Brute-force projective counts of X^d+Y^d+Z^d=W^d equal p^2+p+1+C at (7,3),(13,3),(13,4),(11,5): 99, 261, 108, 405, matching the artifact's point counts.

claims.quote: The number of terms is B=(d-1)(d^2-3d+3), and each has absolute value p
claims.finding: (d-1)^3-(d-1)(d-2)=(d-1)(d^2-3d+3); enumeration gave 6, 21, 52 admissible triples for d=3,4,5 and |J|=p for every one, including the a+b=0 case.

claims.quote: It satisfies e_t+e_(-t)=2 and sum e_t=phi(d)
claims.finding: S_(-t)=3d-S_t and d does not divide S_t when a+b+c is nonzero mod d, so the two floors sum to 1 and e_t+e_(-t)=2; summing over phi(d)/2 pairs gives phi(d).

claims.quote: Thus this primary condition selects the correct root multiple of a balanced generator CLASSICALLY
claims.step: Prime Conductors Need No Phase Oracle
claims.finding: The count p^2-3p+3=1 mod ell and the linear-coefficient argument are correct; a direct check of A(1)=1, A'(1)=0 mod ell on 1398 triples for ell in {3,5,7,11} found no failure, and the 2ell roots +/-zeta^k have distinct residues mod lambda^2.

claims.quote: LLL plus primary normalization reproduces all six prime-conductor native surface controls
claims.finding: Artifact: exactly the d=3,5,7 controls (six) have status CLASSICAL_PUBLIC_IDEAL_RECONSTRUCTION_COMPLETED with matching point counts; the composite d=4,8,9,12 controls do not. The p=2^61-1, d=11 control has 51 profiles, 200 triples, point count equal to p^2+p+1+C, |C|<=910p and C=910 mod 11, and is scoped as a certificate without an LLL success theorem.

summary: Both judges rated the note needs-work on scope only: judge A flagged the bold Decision and judge B the title, and I kept both, since each headline states the classical algorithm or the removal without the status line's condition that the local application is review pending and without saying the Lenstra-Silverberg recovery was never executed. The artifact records classical_known_norm_recovery_executed=false and independent_or_formal_review_completed=false for the 6 small and 51 large controls.

The status line and Next Research Action make it 'subject to independent review of the application', and the Lenstra-Silverberg recovery algorithm was not executed (artifact: classical_known_norm_recovery_executed=false, independent_or_formal_review_completed=false).

claims.quote: Theorem 1.3, gives a deterministic classical polynomial-time decision AND recovery algorithm
claims.finding: Both judges checked the arXiv statement (CM-order, fractional ideal, totally positive w with I*bar(I)=Aw; decide and compute v; no GRH), and the artifact records the same input/output. I did not re-read the paper, so this rests on their agreement.

claims.quote: Since e_t+e_(-t)=2, we have I*bar(I)=product_t P_t^2=p^2*A
claims.finding: Conjugation maps the kernel of zeta->eta^t to that of zeta->eta^(-t), so I*bar(I)=prod P_t^(e_t+e_(-t)); p splits completely since ell|(p-1), so the product is p^2*A with w=p^2 totally positive.

claims.quote: The trace Gram's smallest eigenvalue is1, so each |a_j|<=sqrt(ell-1)*p
claims.finding: Tr(zeta^i zeta^-j) is ell-1 or -1, so the Gram is ell*I-11^T of size ell-1 with eigenvalues ell and 1 (determinant ell^(ell-2), as the note says); a^T G a=(ell-1)p^2 gives sum a^2<=(ell-1)p^2.

claims.quote: Its index is p^(sum e_t+1)=p^ell
claims.finding: sum e_t=ell-1, and |v(1)*Norm_K(J)|=p*p^(ell-1)=p^ell, so containment plus equal index gives equality.

summary: Both judges rated the note sound and agreed on every claim, so there was no disagreement to resolve. I re-checked the load-bearing identities numerically for m=4, c=[2,3,5,7]: A^3=503*I, the H^2|0> coefficient matrix at cut 2 has rank 4 while A^2|0> has rank 3, and the minor on rows/columns (0,1,3,6) equals -4200-8400*omega. I also checked E_r|0>=|r> for all 81 labels, and a random entangled pilot gives identical input and output energies (2.6475836 both). The commutation phases follow from U_l U_j=omega U_j U_l for l>j, and Result 4 is scoped to energy estimation under constructibility and controlled-precision premises.

claims.quote: the one-directional relation gives A^3=(sum c_j^3)I
claims.finding: Numerically A^3=503*I for c=[2,3,5,7] (8+27+125+343), matching the artifact.

claims.quote: minor with EXACT determinant -4200-8400*omega, nonzero in Z[omega]
claims.finding: H^2|0> reshaped 9x9 at cut 2 has rank 4, its (0,1,3,6) minor is -7274.61i = -4200-8400*omega, and the one-directional A^2|0> has rank 3.

claims.quote: no generator is uniform against all remaining predecessors
claims.finding: U_j commutes with U_j^dagger but omega-commutes with every other U_k, and U_k, U_k^dagger carry opposite phases, so for m>=2 no generator can be last.

claims.quote: Thus for ANY normalized pilot, input and output have identical energy expectations
claims.finding: With M=sum psi_r E_r, <psi|H|psi>=Tr(M^dagger H M)/Tr(M^dagger M); a random entangled 4-qutrit pilot gives equal values to 1e-15.

claims.quote: It uses m(m-1)/2+2m ideal logical qutrit Clifford gates
claims.finding: m(m-1)/2 label SUMs plus m Fourier and m SUM gates; the artifact records 5 for m=2 and 9 for m=3.

claims.quote: bond controlled-precision pilot cannot support an ENERGY-estimation separation here
claims.finding: Follows from the intertwiner identity and classical MPS contraction; the premises and the restriction to energy estimation are stated, and the optimum energy is explicitly not claimed easy.

summary: Both judges rated the note sound with identical holds on the radius recurrence, the symmetric spectrum, the outward-rounding width bound, the recursive ground circuit and the dependence counterexample, so there was no disagreement. I re-derived fact 1 (P_j times any product of earlier labels is a nonidentity, traceless Pauli) and fact 2 (an all-anticommuting Q exists by full row rank). The commuting and anticommuting radius updates and the lower-eigenvector angle also check out. The artifact's 512-term certificate has width 165/2^79=330*2^-80 against 341 anticommuting root steps, within the stated bound. ZZI+IZZ+ZIZ has minimum -1, and the falsifier is scoped to ground energy only.

claims.quote: Each eigenspace of H_(j-1) therefore has equal +1/-1 multiplicities for P_j
claims.finding: Spectral projectors of H_(j-1) are polynomials in earlier labels; independence makes P_j times each product a nonidentity Pauli, so P_j is a traceless involution on each eigenspace.

claims.quote: Thus every H_j has a spectrum symmetric about zero
claims.finding: The symplectic map to syndromes is surjective for independent labels, so a Q with all-one syndrome exists and QHQ=-H; hence E_min=-R_m.

claims.quote: R_j = sqrt(R_(j-1)^2 + c_j^2)
claims.finding: Anticommutation with all predecessors cancels the cross terms, giving H_j^2=H_(j-1)^2+c_j^2 I.

claims.quote: so interval width is at most (number of root steps)*2^(-b)
claims.finding: Commuting additions shift both endpoints equally and keep the width a grid multiple; each 1-Lipschitz outward-rounded root adds at most one grid step. Artifact: width 165/2^79=330*2^-80 with 341 root steps.

claims.quote: applies exp(-i theta Z_<j Y_j/2), theta=-atan2(c_j,R_(j-1))
claims.finding: On the block [[-R,c],[c,R]], tan(theta/2)=-c/(R+sqrt(R^2+c^2)) gives the lower eigenvector.

claims.quote: Dependence matters: ZZI+IZZ+ZIZ has ground energy-1, not-3
claims.finding: The product of the three Ising terms is the identity, so they cannot all be -1; the minimum is -1 and the labels sum to zero.

summary: Both judges rated the note needs-work for the same title gap and agreed on everything else, so there was no disagreement to resolve. I confirmed the gap: the title calls the attack a falsifier, while the body limits it to a finite best-of-four versus mean comparison at four predeclared sizes and shows that under its IID premise the attack cannot beat (1+R)/2, below the DQI target. Against the artifact I checked the best scores 7,7/27,27/30,30/105,104 and the 50 forced predicates (exposed prefix 51, 9 free bits, 512 messages) at N=127 and 11 forced (15 free bits, 32768 messages) at N=31. I recomputed the IID tail bound 2048*Pr(Bin(76,1/2)>=53)=0.78293, matching 3610635178399977029/2^62. The first-moment flat bound is 1/2 at t=3, d=2, N=1, as the artifact records.
